title: Recording a calypso album with Robert Mitchum
summary: He describes weeks of rehearsal with Mitchum and Gene DePaul.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: But the guy that I really like that I worked with was Mitchum. We did a calypso album, and we rehearsed for about

a month, every day. And we rehearsed about eleven o'clock in the morning. He had all these... He had just done a picture down in the South Seas somewhere, down around St. Thomas or something, Calypso, and he had all these records. He's a very musical guy -- very musical. Good musically. No skipped beats, all the crap. And we'd go through about four-or-five-six tunes. The guy that wrote the lyrics to "I'll Remember April," Gene DePaul, he was there -- he and Mitchum and me.

And Mitchum's Girl Friday, her name was Reba, and she's out at the desk, in the office. So we go through about six or seven of these tunes, you know, and he'd get a little better at 'em... Finally, all of a sudden, he'd say, "Reba! Three. Make 'em good." Here she'd come with three Bloody Mary's. Then he'd sit back and he'd start telling us stories. And boy, if you think anybody...
He'd say, "Howdy-Dowdy, folks. I used to be a stand-up comic, but now I do all my funny stuff lying down."
